reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement. DTH response to HER2/neu-derived peptides increased in 11/20 patients, with 5/8 DTH-negative patients converting to DTH-positive. This demonstrates immune system engagement with the HER2 target. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear pathway modulation observed. The vaccine induced immune priming (DTH response), trastuzumab engaged HER2 receptor antagonism, and cyclophosphamide achieved lymphodepletion. All three mechanisms showed biological activity. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Excellent clinical translation. Primary safety endpoint was met with manageable toxicity (100% grade 1-2, 0% grade 3+). PFS outcomes were successful across the population (18/20 progression-free overall, 12/12 early stage, 6/8 metastatic). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Both early stage (12/12 progression-free) and metastatic (6/8 progression-free) subgroups responded, though early stage showed numerically better outcomes. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits definitive efficacy assessment, but the combination of safety, immunologic response, and PFS outcomes in a high-risk population supports success.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm design without control group limits definitive efficacy assessment, though multiple positive endpoints support success
